- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–2%.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; reduce initial forecast values by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment shows sudden reversal (e.g., from +0.6 to -0.6 within 3 days), model lags in adjusting; apply correction 2–3 days ahead of true sentiment shift.
- In 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period mean reversion; reduce final 5–7 days of forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect diminishing momentum.
